12522.name: Cam Ward
12522.headline: 0-5 Titans offense sputtering; Ward's sophomore year is stalling
12522.news: Ward went 23-of-36 for 170 yards, no touchdowns and an interception in the 26-3 Week 5 loss to Houston (Oct. 11), taking a season-high four sacks as Tennessee managed 187 total yards. Through five games he has roughly 896 passing yards with a 3:3 TD:INT ratio and a ~63% completion rate. Head coach Robert Saleh said he has not considered a QB change, and OC Brian Daboll has publicly backed him, though media are openly debating a benching (Mitchell Trubisky is the backup). Local film reviews spread the blame across the offensive line, a thin supporting cast and Daboll's red-zone play-calling.
12522.take: In superflex, Ward still holds value simply as a young starting QB with a long runway, but his 2026 production is unstartable and his value is cratering in real time. The context (bad line, new playcaller, rookie WR Carnell Tate still developing) explains some of it, which is why selling for pennies right now is a mistake. For a rebuilding team, he is a reasonable hold-and-hope stash: the downside risk is a benching or a 2027 QB pick, so do not buy aggressively either. Re-evaluate after the trade deadline window based on whether Tennessee shows any signs of progress.

6797.name: Justin Herbert
6797.headline: Herbert turnover-prone behind rookie-laden line as Chargers fall to 0-5
6797.news: In the 23-17 Week 5 loss to Denver (Oct. 11), Herbert completed 14 of 24 for 121 yards, a TD and an INT, ran six times for 54 yards and fumbled twice (one lost) while being sacked five times; WR Quentin Johnston was inactive (chest). Season totals sit around 937 yards, 5 TD and 7 INT on a 59% completion rate with 17 sacks taken. PFF grades him 35th of 36 qualifying QBs, and the Chargers started four rookies on the offensive line. Some reports reference a new offensive coordinator, but that detail is not consistently confirmed across sources.
6797.take: This is the worst stretch of Herbert's career, and it is mostly an environment problem: a rookie offensive line and missing pass catchers. He is still 28 with a long track record of top-tier play, so in superflex his long-term value is far higher than his current production suggests. For a 1-4 rebuilding team, he is the kind of veteran QB contenders still pay for, but selling at the bottom of his value would be poor timing. Hold, and only move him if a contender offers near his pre-season price.

12533.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
12533.headline: Efficient but capped: 'Bill' leads carries, Rachaad White leads snaps
12533.news: In the 27-27 Week 5 tie with the Giants (Oct. 11), Croskey-Merritt ran 11 times for 82 yards including a 33-yard TD on the opening drive, but did not get a carry over the final 14-plus minutes of regulation or overtime. Usage reports show him at roughly a 35% snap share and 16% route share, with Rachaad White out-snapping him 37 to 22 and handling passing downs. Earlier in the season he dipped to nine carries for 15 yards in Week 4. Kaytron Allen, Jerome Ford and recently re-signed Austin Ekeler round out a crowded room.
12533.take: He is the best runner on the roster and gets early-down and scoring work when Washington is in neutral or positive game script, but committee usage with no receiving role caps his weekly ceiling. That makes him a touchdown-dependent RB3/flex in half PPR. In dynasty he is a cheap second-year back with proven efficiency; the team pushed him to become an every-down player in the offseason, and so far that has not happened. Hold rather than sell low; he could become a buy if White or Washington's coaching staff changes.

5967.name: Tony Pollard
5967.headline: Pollard keeps early-down volume on a broken Titans offense
5967.news: Pollard handled 14 of Tennessee's 18 RB carries for 52 yards in the 26-3 Week 5 loss to Houston (Oct. 11). Tyjae Spears out-snapped him 34 to 30 and caught all nine of his targets, taking over the passing-down role. Rookie Nicholas Singleton has played only a small role so far. Pollard is in the final year of the three-year deal he signed in 2024, and he missed some preseason practice time with a foot issue.
5967.take: Pollard's carry share is secure, but he plays in an offense that cannot sustain drives or reach the red zone, and Spears is taking the receiving work that matters in half PPR. That makes him a low-end RB2 or flex with a low ceiling. Start him in weeks where your other options are thin, but do not expect spike weeks. He is a reasonable piece to package in a trade if someone values his steady carries.

8210.name: Chig Okonkwo
8210.headline: Healthy again, Okonkwo led Washington in targets in Week 5
8210.news: After a hamstring issue, Okonkwo practiced fully and was cleared for Week 5 (Oct. 9). He caught 4 of a team-high 6 targets for a season-high 60 yards in the 27-27 tie with the Giants (Oct. 11), but saw only one target after halftime and none in overtime. He signed a three-year deal worth up to $30 million with Washington this offseason and has been described as a de facto No. 2 receiving option behind Terry McLaurin. Washington faces San Francisco in Week 6.
8210.take: The opportunity is real, but his history is that of a high-floor TE2: he has never topped about a 16% target share and has rarely been used near the goal line. Jayden Daniels' return helps, but Daniels' running cuts into short-area targets. In dynasty, at 27 with a new contract, he is a useful bench TE rather than a building block; if a contender values him as a streamer, selling is fine for a rebuilding team.

13301.name: Antonio Williams
13301.headline: Rookie flashes, but production has been modest beyond his debut
13301.news: The third-round rookie from Clemson caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in the Week 5 tie with the Giants (Oct. 11), with Stefon Diggs ruled out. He has a 15-155-1 line on 22 targets through five games, most of it from a 4-64-1 debut against Philadelphia. In Week 4 with McLaurin inactive he drew eight targets but caught only three for 21 yards, and an 87-yard TD was wiped out by a penalty.
13301.take: Williams is getting real snaps on a thin receiving corps, and the volume spikes when veterans are hurt, which is a good sign for a Day 2 rookie. However, his efficiency has been poor apart from one game, and McLaurin and Diggs are ahead of him when healthy. For a rebuilding dynasty team, he is exactly the young asset to keep, since his value is low and the role could grow in 2027. In redraft he is not yet startable.

13274.name: Germie Bernard
13274.headline: Rookie gets first start, leads Steelers in targets with Pittman hurt
13274.news: With Michael Pittman Jr. re-aggravating a foot injury (expected to miss multiple weeks, possible IR), the second-round rookie made his first start in Week 5 (Oct. 11) and posted 6 catches for 80 yards on a team-high 9 targets in the 34-22 win over the Colts. Steelers Depot charted him at 55 snaps (about 92%), and NBC noted he ran a route on 35 of 38 dropbacks. Mike McCarthy praised his ability to play all three receiver spots. He is projected to start again in Week 6 at Tampa Bay.
13274.take: The role is the story: near-full-time snaps and a top target share while Pittman is out. That makes him a viable WR3/flex in 12-team redraft leagues for the next few weeks, with the caveat that one game is a small sample and his role may shrink when Pittman returns. Treat him as a short-term starter, not a locked-in breakout. He is worth holding on the bench for the week-to-week flex upside.

9504.name: Kayshon Boutte
9504.headline: Deep-threat role in Houston offers little fantasy value
9504.news: Boutte, traded from New England to Houston, caught 3 of 5 targets for a season-high 38 yards in the Texans' 26-3 Week 5 win over Tennessee (Oct. 11), including a toe-tap 23-yard grab that kept a TD drive alive. Through five games he has 12 catches on 18 targets for 153 yards and no touchdowns. Nico Collins is back as the focal point, and FantasyPros notes Houston also traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., pushing Boutte further down the pecking order.
9504.take: Boutte is a field-stretching role player with limited volume, and the Harrison Jr. trade makes a meaningful target share unlikely. At this stage he is a deep-league bench body, not a dynasty asset worth a roster spot on a rebuilding team unless your bench is empty. If anyone offers anything for him, take it; otherwise he is a cut candidate for a younger upside stash.

12492.name: Pat Bryant
12492.headline: On IR with ankle injury; out until at least early November
12492.news: Denver placed Bryant on injured reserve with an ankle injury on Oct. 9, ahead of the Week 5 game at the Chargers. He must miss at least four games and cannot return before the Nov. 8 matchup against Carolina, according to Newsweek. Before the injury he had 9 catches for 133 yards and a TD on 12 targets through four games. In dynasty he is a second-year depth piece whose value is low now; hold him in an IR slot if you have one, since selling him while injured gets you nothing. Do not expect a major role even after he returns.

13269.name: Fernando Mendoza
13269.headline: No. 1 pick debuts in mop-up duty; Cousins keeps the job for now
13269.news: Mendoza got his first regular-season snaps in Week 5 (Oct. 11), replacing Kirk Cousins with about six minutes left in a 45-17 loss at New England and going 6-of-8 for 48 yards. The move was not injury-related. On Oct. 12, coach Klint Kubiak said Cousins remains the starter but that the team has confidence in Mendoza if called upon. Kubiak has said the timing of a Mendoza start will hinge on the rookie's own readiness, and Las Vegas (3-2 after two straight losses) hosts Buffalo in Week 6.
13269.take: The rookie hasn't started yet, so for now his value is all about the future. Two straight losses and a blowout cameo make a mid-season switch more likely than it was in September, but nobody has reported a date, and preseason predictions of a Week 6 takeover were only guesses. In a 10-team superflex dynasty league, a No. 1 overall QB with a likely starting job in 2027 has real value for a rebuilding team. He also had a pick-six and some sloppy moments in the preseason, so don't pay a premium as if he's already proven. The best time to buy is now, while managers trying to win this year see him as dead roster space.

12527.name: Ashton Jeanty
12527.headline: Banged-up Jeanty grinding at 3.4 YPC; receiving work keeps him afloat
12527.news: Jeanty was a game-time decision in Week 5 (Oct. 11) with ankle and foot injuries, a flare-up of plantar fasciitis on top of the low ankle sprain he suffered in August camp. He was active and ran 10 times for 27 yards, catching 3 of 6 targets for 50 yards, in a 45-17 loss at New England. Through the first four games he had 78 carries for 264 yards (3.4 YPC) with no rushing TDs, but 19 catches for 165 yards and two receiving scores. He hasn't topped 58 rushing yards since a 102-yard opener, and rookie Mike Washington Jr. has been efficient in a small role (24-120-1 through four games).
12527.take: His volume is still strong, but his efficiency is poor, and two lower-body injuries that keep flaring up are a real concern. The receiving role is growing, which helps his floor in half PPR, but a run game this weak on a struggling offense caps his ceiling. A possible switch to rookie QB Mendoza could make the offense worse in the short term. In dynasty he's still a young bell-cow profile worth holding, so don't sell him for less than he's worth. For Weekend Warriors, only buy him at a discount from a frustrated manager. Don't pay RB1 prices for a player putting up RB2 numbers at less than full health.

9221.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
9221.headline: Gibbs posts 200+ yards, sits at 747 yards and 9 TDs
9221.news: In Week 5 (Oct. 11) against Arizona, Gibbs ran 25 times for 151 yards and two TDs and caught 5 of 6 targets for 56 yards and another score. Through five games he has 747 scrimmage yards and nine touchdowns. With David Montgomery traded to Houston in the offseason and Isiah Pacheco on IR with a back injury, he's the clear workhorse. He signed an extension in September reported at about $22.5M per year. Detroit has its bye in Week 6 and returns in Week 7 against Green Bay.
9221.take: He's living up to his place as the consensus 1.01 and might be outperforming it. With Montgomery gone, he's now getting goal-line and high-volume carries on top of his elite receiving role, which is the best-case fantasy outcome. The only real risk is injury, and the backup committee behind him doesn't threaten his touches. Plan around the Week 6 bye, then start him every week. There's no reason to sell unless someone offers a haul.

9508.name: Tyjae Spears
9508.headline: Pass-down-only role behind Pollard; nine catches for 28 yards
9508.news: In Week 5 (Oct. 11), Spears caught all nine of his targets for only 28 yards and lost a fumble on one of his two carries in a 26-3 loss to Houston. Tony Pollard handled early downs with 14 carries. Through five games Spears has 17 carries for 65 yards and 14 catches for 68 yards. He played through an ankle issue in Week 4 against Baltimore, when he totaled six yards, and RotoBaller noted before Week 5 that Pollard had taken over most of the snaps and production.

The nine-catch line was empty in half PPR (about 7 points), and he's getting almost no carries. Long term, he's heading into the end of his rookie contract with a mixed injury history, and there's little sign Tennessee sees him as the lead back. For a rebuilding dynasty team, sell him for any useful piece if someone is chasing the reception total.

2505.name: Darren Waller
2505.headline: Off the bye; TD-dependent TE2 behind McMillan in Carolina
2505.news: Waller signed a one-year deal with Carolina in August (official Aug. 17) as a situational pass-catching tight end. He scored twice against Atlanta in Week 2, caught 5 of 8 targets for 51 yards in Week 3, and caught 3 of 6 for 36 yards against Detroit in Week 4 (a Sunday night game). In that game Tetairoa McMillan drew 16 targets. Carolina was on bye in Week 5 and faces Philadelphia in Week 6.
2505.take: He's getting a steady 6-8 targets a game, which is playable at a thin TE position, but the yardage has been modest and McMillan dominates the passing game. His spike weeks will depend on touchdowns, and his history of soft-tissue injuries makes him a week-to-week streamer, not a set-and-forget TE1. He's on a one-year deal and is in his 30s, so he has no dynasty value beyond this season. In Weekend Warriors, hold him as a streamer and look for an upgrade at TE if one is on waivers.

13279.name: Carnell Tate
13279.headline: Rookie swings from 9-145 breakout to 1-6 dud
13279.news: The No. 4 overall pick posted a 9-catch, 145-yard game on 12 targets at Baltimore in Week 4. The weak spot is the offense: Ward and the Titans have been inconsistent, which makes him boom-or-bust week to week. 13293.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
13293.headline: Rookie eligible to return from wrist IR in Week 6
13293.news: The third-round rookie (No. 80 overall, USC) fractured his wrist in Baltimore's Week 1 win at Indianapolis and had surgery in mid-September, then went on IR. Coach Jesse Minter called the surgery successful and said Lane has a good chance to return fairly quickly. He's eligible to return for the Oct. 18 game at Cleveland (Week 6). The injury cost him a month of development, though, and Rashod Bateman and Devontez Walker are still in the mix. His size and red-zone profile make him a good dynasty stash on a team with an elite QB. Hold him in dynasty and keep him on IR until he has a clear role. He's not a redraft option yet.

12519.name: Luther Burden
12519.headline: Productive per snap, but part-time snaps cap the year-two breakout
12519.news: Burden caught 4 of 6 targets for 63 yards and added an 11-yard run in the Bears' Week 4 win over the Jets (Oct. 4). RotoBaller noted on Oct. 10 that he had cleared 61% of the snaps in just one of four games, though he out-snapped Kalif Raymond against the Jets for the first time since Week 1. Rome Odunze is the clear snap leader. Burden missed the preseason with a groin injury from August camp but was ready for Week 1. I couldn't verify his most recent game line, so check the latest box score.
12519.take: With DJ Moore traded to Buffalo, the talent and target vacuum are there, and he produces when he's on the field. The problem is that he's still a part-timer behind Odunze, with Colston Loveland also taking targets, so his weekly floor is shaky. Rising snaps against the Jets are the trend to watch. If he becomes a full-time player, his price will jump quickly, so he's a sensible dynasty buy now while his snap share hides his talent.

6801.name: Tee Higgins
6801.headline: Groin/neck injuries limit Higgins to 2-22 in Week 5
6801.news: Higgins injured his adductor/groin on a sideline catch late in the Week 4 loss to Jacksonville and also dealt with a neck issue. He missed two practices before a full session on Friday. He was questionable for Week 5 (Oct. 11) against Miami and played 45 of 64 snaps (70%), catching 2 of 4 targets for 22 yards, both season lows, in a 31-24 win. Before that he had a strong start; one data source shows about 25 catches for 401 yards on 39 targets through four games, though sources disagree on his exact totals.
6801.take: The quiet Week 5 was about injury management, not his role. He still played 70% of the snaps, and he's the clear No. 2 to Ja'Marr Chase in a Burrow-led passing offense. Groin injuries can linger, so watch this week's practice reports. That's also why this is a buying opportunity in Weekend Warriors: a manager looking at a 2-22 line may let him go below his WR2 value. He's on a four-year, $115M deal, so his dynasty value is steady, but at his age I'd hold, not chase.

6904.name: Jalen Hurts
6904.headline: Slow start without A.J. Brown; rushing TDs have dried up
6904.news: Philadelphia lost 19-17 to Jacksonville in London on Oct 11. Hurts went 21-of-40 for 220 yards and a TD with two fumbles, one lost. Through five games he's completing about 58% with an 8:3 TD:INT ratio. As of an Oct 8 projection note he was averaging roughly 16.8 fantasy points and 178 passing yards per game, with only one rushing TD. A.J. Brown was traded to New England in the offseason, Sean Mannion is the new OC, and Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith have been dealing with hamstring injuries.
6904.take: Hurts gets his fantasy value from rushing scores. With one rushing TD so far, he's playing like a mid-QB2 instead of the top-8 per-game QB he was for five straight seasons. The supporting cast is clearly worse: Brown is gone, the line has graded bottom-five in early win-rate data, and the backfield is beat up. Some touchdown regression in his favor is likely, and he's still young enough to matter in superflex. A 1-4 team should only buy him at a real discount, not at his name value.

12490.name: Bhayshul Tuten
12490.headline: Clear lead back for 4-1 Jaguars after 22-carry London game
12490.news: In the 19-17 London win over the Eagles on Oct 11, Tuten carried 22 times for 72 yards. Philadelphia stuffed him for a six-yard loss on fourth-and-goal at the end of the first half. He got far more work than Chris Rodriguez Jr. As of Oct 8 (before that game) he had 60 carries for 277 yards and two TDs through four games, and two more Week 4 touchdowns against the Bengals were wiped out by penalties. PFF had him as its second-highest-graded RB after four weeks, and RotoBaller ranked him RB15 in half PPR.
12490.take: Tuten won the job when Travis Etienne left in free agency and Rodriguez got hurt early in the offseason. He's now getting 17 to 22 carries a week for a winning team. His efficiency dropped in London (3.3 YPC), and he doesn't have a big receiving role yet. Even so, his volume and goal-line chances make him a solid RB2 with upside. He's young and cheap, which is exactly the kind of RB a reloading dynasty team should keep.

13287.name: Jeremiyah Love
13287.headline: No. 3 pick still splitting with Allgeier; 12-22 dud vs. Detroit
13287.news: Arizona lost 45-21 to the Lions on Oct 11. Love ran 12 times for 22 yards, a career low, and didn't catch his only target, with the Cardinals down 24-7 at halftime. He was limited in practice that week with an ankle problem but played. In Week 4 he ran 14 times for 63 yards against the Giants and had 15 touches total. Tyler Allgeier outsnapped him 59% to 43% in Week 1, and reports say that through five games Allgeier has about 40 more pass snaps and a slight overall snap lead.
13287.take: So far the talent hasn't turned into workload. Love averages about 11 carries outside his Week 3 spike and gets almost no targets because Allgeier handles passing downs. Arizona has lost several straight, which leads to negative game scripts that hurt his weekly value. In dynasty this is the right time to buy: he's a No. 3 overall pick with Conner on IR and Benson out for the year, and his managers may be frustrated. In redraft, don't pay an RB1 price for a split-snap back on a bad team.

11577.name: Will Shipley
11577.headline: Partial plantar fascia tear ends spot start; out multiple weeks
11577.news: Shipley started the Oct 11 game in London because Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was out and Tank Bigsby (core muscle surgery) was on IR. He had five carries for six yards and a 2-yard TD before leaving in the second quarter with a foot injury. Per Adam Schefter, it's a partial tear of the plantar fascia, and he could miss multiple weeks. Dameon Pierce took over and ran 11 times for 14 yards. Barkley's status for Week 6 against Carolina is uncertain.
11577.take: Shipley only had value because of the injuries ahead of him, and now he's injured too. He has averaged about 3 yards per carry over his career, and once Barkley comes back he goes back to special teams and occasional touches. Plantar fascia injuries tend to linger. A 4-1 redraft team doesn't need to hold him, so he's a drop unless your bench is very deep.

He's still a young TE with production, so in dynasty you should hold him and not sell at his current low price.

13311.name: Chris Bell
13311.headline: Rookie back from ACL already playing 80%+ of snaps
13311.news: Bell is a third-round pick who tore his ACL in Nov 2025, came off the NFI list in August, and played from Week 1. He caught 4 passes for 67 yards on 7 or 8 targets in Week 3 (sources disagree). In Week 4 he caught none of his 3 targets but played 82% of snaps and ran 85% of routes, second among Miami WRs behind Malik Washington. A long TD that week was called back after he stepped out of bounds. The team has limited his practice reps for his knee, but he wasn't on the final Week 5 injury report (Oct 9). I couldn't find his line from the Oct 11 loss to the Bengals.
13311.take: He's playing a lot, and his route share has gone up every week, which is unusual for a rookie coming off an ACL tear. Miami's passing game with Malik Willis is run-heavy and inconsistent, so his weekly production is a WR5 dart at best this year. In dynasty, the 6'2", 222 lb build and full-time role make him a good stash. His value should keep rising as he gets further from surgery.

7564.name: Ja'Marr Chase
7564.headline: Played through concussion, scored one-handed 45-yard TD; Week 6 bye
7564.news: Chase cleared concussion protocol in time to play in the 31-24 win at Miami on Oct 11. He caught 6 passes for 77 yards, including a one-handed 45-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Before that game he had 21 catches on 28 targets for 212 yards and 3 TDs through four games. That includes a 2-catch, 12-yard opener that the OC later called a mistake in usage. The Bengals are on bye in Week 6 and play at Baltimore in Week 7.
7564.take: Chase is still one of the best receivers in fantasy. He was a first-team All-Pro in 2025 with 125 catches for 1,412 yards, and Burrow is healthy and throwing for four TDs in a game. His slower start in volume is a reason to buy, not a worry. In redraft, his bye week and recent concussion could make his manager willing to sell slightly cheaper. In dynasty, a 1-4 team should only move him for a very large return, because he's 26 and an elite WR who should hold value through the rebuild.

11632.name: Malik Nabers
11632.headline: Career-high 20 targets in Week 5; knee looks fine
11632.news: In the Oct 11 27-27 tie with Washington, Nabers had a career-high 20 targets and caught 11 for 121 yards and a TD per most reports (one outlet says 12-145). That gives him a league-high 27 targets and 233 yards over the last two games. He had soreness in his surgically repaired right knee during the week but had no injury designation. Earlier he complained publicly about not getting the ball after halftime in a win. The Giants play New Orleans in Week 6, and the Saints have allowed about 212 receiving yards per game.
11632.take: This is what managers who drafted him hoped for once he was past the ACL and meniscus surgeries. The Giants are force-feeding him the ball even with Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney on the roster. Knee soreness is worth watching, but his recent workload is elite. Start him every week in your 4-1 redraft league. Selling now could get a good return, but his WR1 production is more valuable to a contender.

11566.name: Jayden Daniels
11566.headline: Back from dislocated elbow, runs for 103 yards and two TDs
11566.news: Daniels dislocated his left elbow in late September, missed two games, and came back in Week 5 (Oct 11) against the Giants. He went 17-of-25 for 199 yards and ran nine times for a team-high 103 yards and two touchdowns in a 27-27 overtime tie. He was still wearing a bulky brace on the elbow during the week. Through three games he has about 459 passing yards with 3 TD and 0 INT, plus roughly 203 rushing yards and 2 TD. Washington plays at San Francisco on Monday night in Week 6.
11566.take: His rushing ceiling is fully back, and that is what makes him a top-10 fantasy QB. The worry is durability. This is the same elbow that ended an attempted comeback early last season, and his running style keeps him exposed to hits. Washington is winless, so he will have to keep pushing the ball and running. In a 12-team 1QB redraft league he stays in your lineup every week. Keep a usable QB2 on the roster as insurance.

9224.name: Chase Brown
9224.headline: Plenty of volume, poor efficiency; Perine out-carried him in Week 5
9224.news: Brown has about 71 carries for 246 yards (roughly 3.5 YPC) and 1 TD through five games, plus a big receiving role. That includes an 11-catch, 71-yard game in the Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. In the Week 5 win over Miami (31-24) he had 13 carries for 39 yards, caught 3 of 4 targets for 21 yards, and lost a fumble. Samaje Perine out-carried him 14-13, gained 68 yards, and caught a red-zone TD. Brown still led in snaps, but only 60% to 51% after having at least a 30-point snap edge in every earlier game. Cincinnati is on bye in Week 6 and plays at Baltimore on Oct 25.
9224.take: His volume is real: he leads the backfield in snaps and is a high-target receiver in a good offense. The rushing efficiency is bad, though, and Week 5 opened a 'Perine should start' debate that could become a true committee if the fumbles and the 3.5 YPC continue. That uncertainty and the bye week make this the right time to buy. Most analysts still expect him to lead the backfield, and his catches give him a PPR-friendly floor. Even at half PPR he is an RB2 the rest of the way. In dynasty he is a young RB with a three-down profile, and his price is down right now.

9757.headline: Leads Saints backfield with Etienne on IR, Kamara's back ailing
9757.news: Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on IR and can't return before Week 9. Alvin Kamara has a back injury: he missed practice on Oct 7, was listed questionable for Week 5, and touched the ball only five times. In the 23-13 Week 5 loss to Minnesota (Oct 11), Miller led the team with 10 carries for 30 yards and scored New Orleans' only TD. He played just about 30% of the snaps but took 56% of the rushing attempts. C.J. Donaldson also took a couple of carries. The Saints host the Giants in Week 6, and Kamara's status was not settled as of Wednesday.

If Kamara sits, Miller could get 15 or more touches. His low snap share and 3.0 YPC show he is not a three-down back, though. Once Etienne is back in Week 9, Miller probably drops to the third RB again. He is in the last year of his rookie deal and has never played more than eight games in a season.

13413.name: Cyrus Allen
13413.headline: Camp star rookie barely used; Reid says more snaps coming
13413.news: Kansas City took Allen in the fifth round (No. 176) out of Cincinnati. He was one of the stars of training camp and got first-team reps with Mahomes. His preseason was quiet: 6 catches on 12 targets for 39 yards. In the regular season he has been nearly invisible: one offensive snap in Week 1, three in Week 3, and about 10 total snaps through four weeks with one or two targets (reports differ) and no catches. The camp hype is what gives him value, so if a leaguemate still rates him highly, getting a future pick for him is fine. Otherwise keep him in a deep roster spot while you rebuild and watch his snap counts.

9488.news: Through five games JSN has 37 catches on 50 targets for 583 yards (116.6 per game) and 7 TD, which leads the NFL in receiving yards. 11628.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
11628.headline: Traded to Houston; reunites with Stroud, debuts in London
11628.news: On Oct 11, Arizona traded Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick to Houston for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder. He passed his physical on Oct 12. His price is near its lowest after the bad Arizona start, and he is 24 with a WR2-type 2024 season (885 yards, 8 TD) on his record. 6804.name: Jordan Love
6804.headline: Love breaks out of early slump with 367-yard demolition of Bears
6804.news: Through the first three weeks Green Bay started 1-2, capped by a 35-14 primetime loss to Atlanta, with Love under constant pressure and posting career-low completion percentage and passer rating (Chicago Sun-Times, Oct 8). On Oct 11 (Week 5) he went 25-of-31 for 367 yards and two TDs with no picks in a 31-7 rout of Chicago, both scores going to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden also clearing 100 yards. PFF graded him 94.5, the top passing grade of the week. Next up is a Sunday night home game against Dallas in Week 6.
6804.take: The early-season problems looked more like protection and run-game failures than a Love regression, and the Bears game showed the ceiling is intact when he has time. One great game does not erase four weeks of shaky line play, so expect some volatility, but the Dallas matchup sets up as a shootout. In superflex dynasty he is a locked-in starter signed through 2029 with a deep young receiver room, which is exactly the kind of asset a rebuilding team should keep. In 1QB redraft he is a matchup-based starter, not a weekly lock.

13337.headline: Rookie stuck behind workhorse Kenneth Walker in Kansas City
13337.news: The fifth-round Nebraska rookie won the RB2 job in camp and debuted in Week 1 with 8 carries for 24 yards and 2 catches for 44 on 25 snaps while Kenneth Walker ran for 173. What he does offer is contingent value: if Walker misses time, Johnson is the most likely beneficiary in a good offense. For a rebuilding dynasty team he is a cheap stash worth holding rather than selling for scraps, but don't pay up for him.

7567.news: Tampa Bay signed Gainwell to a two-year, $14 million deal this offseason, and camp reports (NBC Sports, Aug 9) had him working mainly as a receiving back. At his age and with a modest contract, he has little dynasty upside for a rebuilding roster. Move him if anyone will give you anything; otherwise he's a bench handcuff.

11604.news: Bowers had a meniscus trim right before the season and has missed time, playing three games so far. Long term, a young TE with this target share is a cornerstone asset, and the arrival of Mendoza doesn't change his role. Don't sell low because of the knee; he is worth more to a rebuild than almost anything you'd get back.

10859.news: LaPorta had back surgery for a herniated disc after a 2025 season cut short at nine games, and was fully cleared before 2026 training camp (ESPN, July). He is in the final year of his rookie deal, and local outlets are already talking about an extension.
10859.take: The back looks like a non-issue so far, with steady targets and touchdowns in a high-scoring offense. The ceiling is capped somewhat by competition for targets in Detroit, so he is more of a reliable mid-to-high TE1 than a weekly smash play. As a redraft buy target in Weekend Warriors, he makes sense if his manager values him like a mid-tier TE, but don't pay a premium after a spike week. In dynasty, a healthy 25-year-old TE in a great offense is worth holding, with the contract year as a minor wrinkle.

13417.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
13417.headline: Rookie on IR after ankle surgery, targeting late-season return
13417.news: Stribling impressed in the preseason with 11 catches for 109 yards across two exhibition games. He played 21 of the first 26 offensive snaps in Week 1 against the Rams without a target before injuring his ankle (deltoid sprain). He had surgery on Sept 16 and was placed on IR; Kyle Shanahan estimated close to 10 weeks and said the team expects him back this season. That timeline points to roughly late November.
13417.take: This season is mostly a write-off; even when he returns he was behind Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey in the pecking order. The real value is 2027 and beyond, when the 49ers' veteran pass catchers age out. For a rebuilding dynasty team, holding a talented rookie at depressed injured value is better than selling him for pennies. In redraft he is irrelevant.

9500.name: Josh Downs
9500.headline: Downs volume capped in a struggling Colts passing game
9500.news: In Week 5 on Oct 11, Downs caught 3 of 6 targets for 47 yards in a 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh. He ran a route on most dropbacks but finished fourth on the team in targets behind Keenan Allen, Tyler Warren and Laquon Treadwell, with Daniel Jones struggling all season (NBC Sports). Alec Pierce is injured, which has narrowed the target tree. Indy hosts winless Tennessee in Week 6, a matchup projected for roughly eight targets.
9500.take: Downs is a talented slot receiver, but in this offense he is fighting for scraps behind a veteran Allen and a rookie TE in Warren, with weak QB play capping everyone. He is a WR3/flex in good matchups like Tennessee rather than a reliable weekly starter. In dynasty he is a useful mid-tier piece; a rebuilding team could move him for a pick or younger asset if a contender values him as a PPR depth piece. Don't buy into a bounce-back narrative until the QB situation improves.

10232.name: Michael Wilson
10232.headline: MHJ trade makes Wilson Arizona's undisputed WR1
10232.news: Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston around Week 5 for 2027 Day 2 and late-round picks (ESPN/Athlon); Harrison was inactive against Detroit. Wilson caught 4 of 7 targets for 30 yards and threw a 7-yard pass in the 45-21 Week 5 loss to the Lions, well short of bullish projections. Even so, he has 30 targets over the last two weeks, up from 14 across Weeks 1-2, and he led all Arizona receivers in snaps. He signed a three-year, $75 million extension this offseason.
10232.take: The volume is real and should stay that way, since Harrison is gone and only Trey McBride competes with him for targets. Efficiency is the issue with Jacoby Brissett-level QB play, so expect high-floor PPR weeks rather than consistent spikes. In Weekend Warriors he is a weekly flex with WR2 upside; the Week 6 matchup with the Rams is fine for a flex start. Don't panic over the 30-yard dud, as the role matters more than one box score.
